questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: having a big exchange student culture as well as accessibility and relevance. My institute had allocated spots which made the chance of me getting in bigger. I also wanted to go somewhere where i already knew somethings about the country as well as knowing that i could easily communicate with other students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Train strikes made it harder, but the university had warned me about this beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had arranged for students to me available in the airport to show new arrivals to the correct train, but due to train strikes they couldnt be there. This was communicated in advance and other options had been presented by the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard! got lucky through a facebook post. Lots of groups exists for finding housing in utrecht but there are lots of scammers and desperate students/workers

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can quickly feel quite isolated if you dont find other students to live with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very limited housing were available through the university, and the booking of these became available long after a lot of different preparations and applying for the Erasmus grant were already done. It might not be as attractive to go to Utrecht if you dont get a student dorm, and they send emails to try to persuade you from going at all, but the timing of it makes it very hard to stop the process.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In the initial description of the University they link to their website where they have the courses available listed. Very easy to see what the possibilities are.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have a great and helpful international student center which you can email with questions and they will help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I experienced no cancellations. I wanted to change course once i got there but i was too late. I think it would have been easily possible if i were quicker.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the requirements for each course in the course catalog so you know what kind of pre-knowledge is expected and you wont be overwhelmed. If the course is not for you when you get there, be quick to email the international student office and inquire about a change.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3rd year BA courses,

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Somewhat different grading criteria and focus than what im used to. More closed-book and focus on remembering specific terms/formulas

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to functional programming
Data analytics
Introduction to financial mathematics 
Introduction to machine learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend data analytics, as they are a pretty new course and doesnt rely on any other course at the university. 

I would recommend functional programming if you are a data science student or programmer and want to expand you codeing skills. Would not recommend if you just want to learn to code. 
I would not recommend Introduction to machine learning or Introduction to financial mathematics unless a math student and really interested in the mathematical formulas behind both concepts. 
They build upon theory that i dont think ive been exposed to before even though i thought i had the prerequisites necessary.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Because of the inflation, electricity was way more expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transport were more expensive than i thought. I think there was some ways to save on that, but not too easy to figure out. 

Wine very cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have lots of clubs and student associations that are promoted and made visible the first couple of weeks. Sometimes a bit hard to find them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: buddygodutch is an association that helps putting internationals in contact with duchies and host cheap social activities. Not always successful but a good way meet new people. Have an academic counterpart as well. They also have student associations connected to almost every course direction as well as dance clubs mm.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend joining ESN and/or buddyGoDutch to meet other international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Very easy to get around the netherlands, so could visit other cities such as amsterdam, ammersford or rotterdam. There are also lots of museums. If going in the summer/spring, canal tours are also available.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, although the Dutch can be a bit hard to become close with

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a student association, but be aware that few international students show up

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dutch students seem to stick to themselves which makes it hard to get to know locals. And although they bike a lot, the attitude towards bicyclist is a bit different and the biketracks are often both ways

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Beautiful cities with canals running through.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be on the lookout for accommodations from the beginning and be sure to have somewhere to go when you arrive. Will recommend stayokay hostle in the middle of Utrecht center. 

Bike paths are often two-ways so be sure to look both ways before crossing. Also bikes will not stop for pedestrians. 

Find a bike. Bike rental is pretty easy and often other students will have a voucher.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not all places take foreign cards, and some of these places dont take cash either so make sure to check. You can get a maestro card (which they take everywhere they take cards) through revolut even if you dont want to open a dutch bank account

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being on your own and learning new things about yourself and get the chance to immerse yourself in an other culture and city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Finding people to meet with on a regular basis while also making sure to meeting new people and try new things. I think this will be easier if living in a student dorm. 
(also housing is very very difficult)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
